title: BRONZE FOR THE PLACE OF SACRIFICE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The bronze from the wave offering was 70 talents and 2,400 shekels. They used it to make the bases for the entrance to the tent of meeting, the bronze altar with its bronze grating and all its utensils, the bases for the surrounding courtyard and those for its entrance and all the tent pegs of the tabernacle and those for the surrounding courtyard." - Exod 38:29-31 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter ends with bronze, and where it went is worth noticing.

Bronze went to the altar, the courtyard bases, the entrance bases and the tent pegs. Everything that touched the ground, took the fire, or sat at the outer edge. Gold was reserved for the innermost places; bronze did the work at the boundary and in the flames.

Bronze withstands heat. God assigned the metal that could take burning to the place where burning happened.

He still does this. He does not send us into hard places without fitting us for them. His grace is sufficient, and His power is made perfect in weakness (2 Cor 12:9). If you are standing somewhere that feels like fire, He has not misjudged what you can bear.

And notice how the chapter closes: with tent pegs. Not with the ark or the altar, but with the smallest items on the list. A full accounting, right down to the pegs.

That is the character of this whole chapter. Every material weighed. Every worker named. Every peg counted. Nothing casual, nothing lost, nothing beneath God's attention.

Your life is being accounted for with the same care.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What hard place has God equipped you for without your realising it?
2. Do you believe God notices the smallest details of your faithfulness?
3. Where do you need to trust that He has not misjudged what you can bear?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You equip me for the places You send me. Nothing about my life escapes Your care. Amen.
